title: Finding a weight: a stop at 3 reps left on every ramp set, and bigger steps on light free weights outside the risk groups (Phase 4 Part 2)
summary: Two changes to CAL-001, the weight-finding ramp. (1) The Product Owner's choice on 19 Oct 2026 (D-116, option C of the Part 2 report): when the equipment has no step inside the +20-30% band (2.5 -> 5 kg dumbbells is +100%), a rating of '5+' takes the next step, up to double the load, on free weights as already on machine stacks (D-070) - but only for someone who is not a beginner, is under 60, has a standard screening and no health condition; everyone else keeps the band and the start weight becomes the working weight. (2) Found while measuring (1): the bands alone don't keep a ramp set within RPE 8. At a 10-rep ramp set, +10-15% after '4 more' is about 5 reps fewer (Epley), so the next set ends near failure; in a 12-week simulation of an experienced lifter about 1 ramp set in 10 went past RPE 8 and 16 of 34 ramps ended 'too hard', with or without (1). Every ramp set now stops at its target reps or with about 3 reps left, whichever comes first; RIR 3 is already CAL-001's working-load rating, and the reps done give the working load or its estimate (INT-004), as D-115 already reads them. With honest ratings, ramp sets past RPE 8 fall to about 1 in 100. MINOR: new parameters and wording inside CAL-001's existing limits (never above RPE 8, at most 5 ramp sets, sessions 1-4).

changed_rules.reason: The PO's option C for light free weights (D-116), with the risk groups kept on the band; and a stop at 3 reps in reserve on every ramp set, because the bands alone let about 1 ramp set in 10 go past RPE 8 in simulation (Phase 4 Part 2).
changed_rules.statement: Conservative start; each ramp set is done to its target reps or until about 3 reps are left, whichever comes first; after each set RIR 5+ -> +20-30%, 4 -> +10-15%, 3 -> working load (with the reps done giving its estimate where valid), <=2 -> stop and use -5% next time; <=5 ramp sets; never above RPE 8; confirm at second exposure. When the equipment has no step inside the band, at RIR 5+ the next step is taken, up to double the load: on machine stacks for everyone, and on free weights for someone who is not a beginner, is under 60, has a standard screening and no health condition; otherwise the load is the working load.
changed_rules.uncertainty: Expert Practice. The stop relies on effort ratings, which run about one rep conservative at 12 reps or fewer (Halperin 2022), so 'about 3 left' is usually 3-4 from failure; ratings far from failure ('5+') are less accurate, and the bigger step on free weights relies on them, so it is kept from beginners, people aged 60 or over, gentle mode and anyone with a health condition, and the next set's own stop and rating still govern. Low-rep ramps (3-5 reps) can still end harder after a +25% step from '5+' (1 set in about 100 in simulation). Simulation effects are with honest raters.
